iPhone 18 Pro is about to launch, and with this year's lineup shake-up, it will serve as Apple's de facto standard model like never before.

Without a base iPhone 18, the iPhone 18 Pro becomes Apple's new standard model this year.

For years, Apple has released multiple new iPhones each year, and will no doubt continue to do so for years to come.

However, at Apple's event this week, the iPhone lineup is set for a major shake-up.

Rather than the usual choice between a standard 'iPhone' and 'iPhone Pro,' Apple will be without a base iPhone 18.

Multiple sources indicate that Apple has delayed the launch of the iPhone 18, along with the iPhone Air 2, to early 2027. As a result, this fall's lineup will only include:

With the iPhone 18 pushed back past its usual launch window, the iPhone 18 Pro essentially becomes Apple's new standard model.

Users looking for a more affordable device can still pick up last year's iPhone 17, iPhone 17e, or iPhone Air. However, none of the marketing from Apple and its carrier partners this fall and holiday season will feature an 'iPhone 18' as the new standard to upgrade to — instead, the iPhone 18 Pro fills that role.

The iPhone Ultra will be priced too high to be anything more than a niche option in comparison.

So for the average consumer looking to buy a 'new iPhone,' Apple is essentially offering just two choices: the iPhone 18 Pro and the iPhone 18 Pro Max.

It's an interesting gamble that could make the iPhone 18 Pro the best-selling new Pro model yet, but combined with expected price increases, it's also a risky one for Apple. Potential upgraders may hold onto their existing iPhones longer, given there's no iPhone 18 to upgrade to.

Either way, we'll soon find out whether Apple's new strategy pays off.

What do you think of Apple's changes to the iPhone lineup this year? Let us know in the comments.
